title: DreamGUI
description: DreamGUI builds Unreal UI screens from text. A .dui file under the project's DUI/ folder is the source of one widget Blueprint, named by its first line (class /Game/UI/WBP_Menu): nodes in a tree (Widget, Text, Image, Native.Button...), each with its properties, layout boxes attached with + VerticalBox { }, styles and components. Use this tool to check a source, compile it, see where every node lands at a viewport size with the problems that shows (layout), draw it (preview), read diagnostics, and look up the names the compiler accepts. Read the language reference before writing a screen, look names up instead of guessing them, and run layout after every change: a screen that compiles can still be laid out wrong.

reference.title: The .dui language: everything a screen is written with
A worked example: a settings screen in three files
Pitfalls: what compiles and still comes out wrong
Controls: every Native.* control and what it is for
Diagnostics: every DUInnnn code, what it means and how to fix it

actions.name: check
actions.description: Read a .dui the way the compiler does and report its errors. It builds nothing and writes nothing. Run it after every edit: it is the fastest test.

file.description: The .dui, relative to the project root, e.g. DUI/Menu.dui

all.description: Check every .dui of the project and its plugins instead of one file

actions.name: compile
actions.description: Build the widget Blueprint the file's class line names, creating it when it does not exist, and first every component the file places with use "X.dui" as X. Writes assets: in the user's editor they stay in memory until the user saves them; in a host they are saved.

file.description: The .dui, relative to the project root

force.description: Compile even what has not changed since the last compile

actions.name: diagnostics
actions.description: The errors and warnings this engine already holds from the last check or compile of each file, without compiling anything. Without file: every file that has some.

file.description: The .dui, relative to the project root

actions.name: lookup
actions.description: Find the names the compiler accepts: node types, components (+ VerticalBox), properties with their types and defaults, enum values, events and view model classes. An exact name gives its full entry, Type.Property one property; otherwise a list of names containing the text.

name.description: A name or part of one: Text, Native.Button, VerticalBox, Text.FontSize, Anchor, Widget (what every node has), slot (what @slot takes)

kind.description: Search only this kind of name; default any

actions.name: layout
actions.description: Compile the screen and lay it out at a viewport size, without drawing it. Lists every node with its rect in pixels, whether it shows, its text and whether that fits, then the problems: off the screen, text cut, too small to press, controls on top of each other, edges that nearly line up, sizes that break. Writes the Blueprint as compile does.

file.description: The .dui, relative to the project root

sizes.description: More viewports to try, comma separated, e.g. "1280x720, 2560x1440, 1080x1920": what breaks at only some of them is reported

root.description: List only this node and what is under it: its path (Root/Card) or its id

depth.description: How many levels of the tree to list; default 6

force.description: Compile even when nothing has changed

actions.name: preview
actions.description: Compile the screen and draw it at a viewport size into one PNG, with figures a model can read without seeing it: how much of the viewport it covers, its colours, how bright, and texts that are hard to read against what is behind them. Writes the Blueprint as compile does.

file.description: The .dui, relative to the project root

background.description: What is behind the screen: #RRGGBB, or checker to see what is see-through; default #1C1E26

time.description: Seconds the screen runs before the first picture, so what animates by itself moves; default 0

frames.description: Pictures over duration, side by side in one PNG; default 1

duration.description: Seconds the frames are spread over; default 1

force.description: Compile even when nothing has changed

actions.name: info
actions.description: The plugin and engine versions, the source folders, and what this engine process can do (the user's editor or a host, draws or not).
